acceptance.requirement: The ledger and every event use versioned machine schemas and carry the complete source, repository, payload, evidence, sequence, identity, time, and hash-chain fields.
Every state-changing transition is represented by one machine transition rule; old investigated, ready, review, verifying, deliverable, and delivered authority is removed.
Every frozen test contract requires a digest-valid verified dispatch receipt before implementation starts; discovery actorRole values cannot opt out of the universal gate.
Implementation is one implementing-self-testing attempt whose private red/green log may contain multiple failures without increasing global reworkCount.
Candidate-green binds issue-orchestration.implementer-self-test-receipt.v1 and the unchanged frozen test contract; obsolete verified-candidate receipts cannot satisfy the stage.
Candidate-green cannot become behavior-green without a fresh independent test-owner receipt bound to the same candidate SHA.
Independent rejection returns to the same implementation attempt or an explicit continuation, increments global reworkCount once, and preserves first-failure evidence.
UI/UX issues require an independent UX accepted receipt before documentation or delivery.
UX rejection returns only to the same UI/UX implementation owner and retains low implementation effort.
Documentation can start only after behavior-green for non-UI work or ux-accepted for UI/UX work, and cannot erase an earlier behavior failure.
Delivery cannot start before documentation-green and issue closure requires delivery completion plus machine cleanup completion.
Cleanup failure or quarantine cannot release a slot or lease, enter closed, or overwrite the first failure.
Empty state plus ledger replay deterministically reconstructs node status, attempt, reworkCount, terminal data, evidence keys, timestamps, and a stable projection digest.
Sequence, eventId, attempt creation, runId, nodeId, base SHA, previous digest, payload digest, event digest, deletion, and ordering tampering fail closed.

Cancellation, timeout, invocation failure, environment failure, contract dispute, external block, and resource failure remain distinct auditable events and later success cannot overwrite the first failure.
Historical events cannot be edited for correction; a correction is a new hash-chained event referencing the original event.
A durable event with a missing/stale projection is replayed, while a projection ahead of the ledger is discarded and rebuilt.
A truncated or corrupt ledger tail fails closed, reports the final valid sequence, and does not dispatch or skip the bad event.
Recovery does not repeat an already completed implementation attempt, delivery side effect, commit, or cleanup action.
Terminal entry and recovery require a legal category, direct evidence, and a changed recovery fingerprint; an unchanged fingerprint cannot redispatch.
Issue reopen is an event that invalidates closed projection, clears release authority, and marks dependency/frontier recomputation required.
Only the root scheduler appends verified candidate events; implementer, test owner, UX verifier, documentation writer, cleanup verifier, subagent, and old reviewer cannot write the ledger directly.
The ledger lives only below the validated external state root and never below or above either repository, common workspace, or worktree.
Ledger append, replay, recovery, rejection, and cleanup leave tracked and untracked state of both repositories, the common workspace, and worktrees unchanged.
Group session and member projection are replay-only; every member retains its own test, lease, candidate, verification, commit, and delivery state.
Illegal group order, duplicate active member, and one lease bound to multiple members fail closed.
Semantic DAG proposal events are accepted only after a remote live snapshot change and never from local stage or rework events.
